external_primary_sources.relevant_mechanism: immutable artifact/resource identity by cryptographic digest; stable name may accompany digest
attestation subject is bound to artifact digest
verifiable provenance connects produced artifact to where/when/how it was built
archive inputs require stable ordering independent of filesystem/locale
timestamps are a major source of build nondeterminism
ZIP entries carry container metadata beyond extracted payload bytes

source_level_findings: Current F2 release manifest cryptographically binds the extracted file inventory, file sizes and file SHA-256 values plus source/release/build metadata.
Current external prehandoff receipt binds the release-manifest SHA-256 but does not bind the SHA-256 or byte length of the outer distributed ZIP artifact.
Current clean-machine observation binds the manifest digest and receipt reference but does not recompute/bind the pre-extraction archive digest.
Therefore extracted payload equivalence and exact distributed archive identity are distinct evidence predicates.
The smallest reusable external mechanism is artifact-subject digest binding; full SLSA/in-toto adoption is not justified by this E1 result.
counterhypothesis_note: Existing manifest+receipt is sufficient to protect the extracted payload relation currently tested, but not sufficient to establish byte identity/reproducibility of the exact final ZIP named by the WP1110 frontier.
